title: Inquest set for man killed by police; SIU says driver fled RIDE checkpoint, was shot after his truck struck officer
article: An inquest will be held into the death of an Ottawa-area man who died after being shot by police during a routine traffic stop in Brockville on July 3, 2009.
Phillip Jeffrey Charbonneau, 35, was stopped by the Ontario Provincial Police at the Highway 401 offramp at County Road 29 in Brockville as part of a RIDE program traffic check.

According to the Special Investigations Unit, Charbonneau fled the scene in his pickup and officers followed, eventually blocking his truck with their vehicles, resulting in a collision. The officers then had an "interaction" with the man and "at some point the truck struck an officer," according to the SIU.
Two officers fired their guns and Charbonneau was killed.
According to court records, Charbonneau had an outstanding $5,000 fine for driving while under suspension.

The infraction was the fourth Highway Traffic Act offence listed in court records for Charbonneau, who had been convicted of two counts of speeding and one count of careless driving from March 2007 to October 2008.

Charbonneau's family released a statement in July 2009, mourning the loss of a loved one "in the prime of his life" and saying nothing they had heard so far justified the use of deadly force by police.

An inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act, and will examine the circumstances surrounding Charbonneau's death. It will begin Sept. 26 at the Brockville Court House and is expected to last 10 days.
